chapter_title: Chương 148: Cuối cùng, Quỹ Đầu tư Mạo hiểm đã Đến

segments.title: Chương 148: Cuối cùng, Quỹ Đầu tư Mạo hiểm đã Đến
segments.content:
Chapter 151 0148 The Real Venture Capital Finally Arrives In a large classroom in the Second Teaching Building, Chen Guiliang was listening to the lecture attentively while messaging Senior Sister Ao.

To avoid disturbing other students, his phone was on silent mode.

"Feng Chujun, the owner of TT Music, came for a visit. He said he wants to ask us to upload 'The Wind Rises' to TT Music."

"Is it legitimate?"

"If it wasn't, they would have just uploaded it themselves in violation of the rules. They wouldn't need to ask for our consent."

Ao Yanchen added another message: "He wants to chat with you."

"Who is this person? I mean, what's his background?"

"A Master's in Sociology from Peking University, an old alumnus of ours. He used to be a researcher at the Society for Research on Economic System Reform. The society's supervising body is the Commission for Economic System Reform."

"My class ends in ten minutes. You can entertain him for a bit."

"He wants to have a look around Peking University and asked which classroom you're in."

"I'm in Room 101 of the Second Teaching Building. You can give him my phone number."

Feng Chujun graduated from Peking University with a master's degree in 1987, having studied under Fei Xiaotong.

He hadn't been back to Peking University in many years. Feng Chujun rented a bicycle and leisurely roamed around the campus.

"Senior Brother Feng, where are you?"

"Near Centennial Hall."

"I'll be right there."

The two rode their bikes and met in front of Centennial Hall, then went to a nearby cafe to chat.

After a few pleasantries, Chen Guiliang asked, "Senior Brother Feng's TT Music just went online?"

"It went online at the end of last year," Feng Chujun explained. "Because we insist on providing legitimate music and have strict reviews for song uploads, we haven't been able to scale up."

No wonder Bian Guanyue hadn't found this TT Music at all when she was searching for music platforms.

Chen Guiliang asked curiously, "I heard Senior Brother Feng used to work at the Society for Research on Economic System Reform?"

"That's right. It was called the Research Institute for Economic System Reform back then," Feng Chujun said with a smile. "After researching so many things, I couldn't resist plunging into the business world to try my luck. I've sold electronics, started a newspaper, done consulting, and even dabbled in real estate. Netfrog Music was also founded by me. How should I put it? My personal bottom line is a bit too high, so I'm not really cut out for business."

Netfrog Music, which Feng Chujun founded, also dealt in legitimate music and had even received investment from Sanjiu Group.

But due to severe losses, he was kicked out of the company he founded last year.

After that, Netfrog Music relaxed its song upload review process. Although its user agreement also had some ambiguous clauses, its methods were still much more decent than Decibel Net's.

After chatting aimlessly with him for a while, Chen Guiliang realized that Feng Chujun understood the situation better than anyone and knew that his model of legitimate music would be difficult to grow.

"Then why did you start another company, TT Music?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Feng Chujun said, "The government is about to clean up the music platforms. Perhaps this is an opportunity."

His information was really up-to-date, able to predict the moves from above.

In another month, the National Copyright Administration would issue the "Measures for Administrative Protection of Copyright on the Internet." One of its provisions would be to urge major music platforms to remove works with unclear copyrights and to strengthen copyright supervision.

Feng Chujun put too much faith in the power of policy; he was destined to fail.

Disheartened, he would return to the Society for Research on Economic System Reform next year. He would research social transformation, social stability, social psychology, the urban-rural integration evaluation system, and so on, later becoming the deputy director of "China Reform" magazine.

What would truly kill legitimate music platforms like TT Music wasn't some unscrupulous profiteer like Decibel Net, but QQ Music and Baidu MP3!

Baidu MP3 was even more incredible. It used web crawlers to grab songs from other platforms directly and even routed them through servers in the United States. They didn't produce music, nor did they make money from it; they were merely porters of music on the internet.

Under the pincer attack of these two, legitimate music websites found it difficult to survive.

Only a top-tier legitimate company like Jiutian Music Net could continue to live on.

Because Jiutian Music Net had money. It had received venture capital from IDG last year and had taken the opportunity to cooperate with traditional record companies, purchasing the online copyrights for a large number of songs. It could also organize offline performance events.

After beating around the bush for a long time, Feng Chujun finally stated his purpose: "Besides asking your company to upload 'The Wind Rises' to TT Music, I also want to hold an event with Xiaonei Wang."

"What kind of event?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Feng Chujun said, "Using Xiaonei Wang's story relay feature, we'll hold an 'Online Original Music' contest. We'll invite Xiaonei Wang users to upload their original works to TT Music. The winners will receive prize money, and I can also help them with color ringtones and offline performances. I'd also like to ask Xiaonei Wang to help promote that TT Music's user agreement is the most rigorous and legitimate one on the entire internet!"

"Is this a paid or unpaid event?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Feng Chujun said, "I will pay Xiaonei Wang 100,000 yuan as an event fee."

His funds were limited; this was all he could offer. The rest of the money had to be reserved for running the company.

"A pleasure doing business with you," Chen Guiliang said, very pleased.

This was the first time someone had actively approached Xiaonei Wang to discuss a business collaboration.

The situation was gradually getting better.

Feng Chujun asked, "How about you show me around the campus? I haven't been back to Peking University in over ten years, and many places have been renovated and changed."

"Let's go, Senior Brother Feng." Chen Guiliang was happy to be a tour guide, treating it as keeping a client company.

With the boost from Xiaonei Wang's story relay event and promotional posts on major websites, the spread of "The Wind Rises" was incredibly fast.

Especially the Flash animation MV, after being uploaded to Flash Empire, its views and downloads soared.

The lyrics were a huge plus, resonating with young people.

The individual and the world, growth and insight, youth and memory, maturity and letting go... To put it more simply, it was my feelings, fantasies, and expectations for love, for the past, and for the future.

Some people felt nothing when they heard it, just thinking the song was okay.

But a large number of young people, not just students, but also white-collar workers, loved this song to their very bones.

The more of a文艺青年 (wényì qīngnián) you were, the more of a petty bourgeois, the more you loved this damn song.

After downloading it, they listened to it over and over, actively recommended it to friends, and embedded the audio into their blogs and journals.

Including Decibel Net, pirated versions started appearing on major music platforms after just two or three days.

Chen Guiliang published a statement on Xiaonei Wang: "'The Wind Rises · Xiaonei Wang's Anthem' is the true name of this song. The lyricist and composer permit netizens' use and derivative creation, but engaging in commercial activities without authorization is prohibited. Commercial activities include, but are not limited to..."

Immediately after, Chen Guiliang also published a "Solemn Statement" in the form of a small column in several newspapers.

But it still couldn't stop websites and individuals from ignoring the law!

"Damn it, a rearranged version has appeared on Decibel Net!" Xie Yang had been monitoring the situation. Chen Guiliang had recently hired a subordinate for him.

Now, Xie Yang had his own three-person team, leading his two generals into battle on the internet every day.

Rearranging the music was considered derivative creation, which Chen Guiliang allowed, but on the condition that it was not for commercial activities.

Would Decibel Net listen?

Probably in a little while, Decibel Net would start managing the color ringtone for "The Wind Rises." It didn't matter if they lost the lawsuit; the compensation and fines would be very low, far less than the money they would make from the ringtone.

But they didn't know that the "Measures for Administrative Protection of Copyright on the Internet" was about to be promulgated.
